name: battle-opening-hud-compare
label: The HUD and the backdrop through a battle's opening, canon above and this build below: 44 consecutive frames, 0 pixels, every frame compared rather than sampled. The backdrop is not just a scrolling picture -- it also ANIMATES, on the same scripted engine the overworld uses, ten four-frame steps then nineteen eight-frame ones over a 192-frame loop, and this build had been running a uniform 56-frame loop instead. The scroll matters to the pixel too: canon writes a logical shift of a counter that falls, which rounds the opposite way from a plain divide and puts the whole layer one pixel out on odd frames. The check that first said this matched was sampling every fourth frame, and every fourth frame was exactly the set that already agreed.

name: wave-panel-light-compare
label: The shockwave's panel light, canon (sterile) above and this build below, backgrounds only so the wave's own sprite is hidden and only the yellow highlight it leaves on each panel shows: 90 frames, 0 pixels. This was the last non-zero check in the suite. The hop itself was never the hard part -- what took three attempts was the ends of a segment's life. A hop spawns a NEW segment and abandons the old one where it is, and our build was destroying the abandoned one a frame before it could show its final animation frame, and lighting the newly spawned one a frame late. The real ROM has the same asymmetry in its own code: the handler that runs on a segment's first tick builds its sprite and collision data and never highlights, and highlighting only begins on the tick after.

name: mettaur-attack-compare
label: The Mettaur's whole 70-frame attack cycle, canon (sterile) left and this build right: 0.0 pixels a frame. It hides, swings, and sends a shockwave down the row. The virus acts on an RNG neither side shares, so there is no fixed offset to compare on -- the two are aligned by finding the lag that lines up the frames on which its own bounding box changes, and 16 of the canon side's 17 boundaries land exactly. This was the last animated residue: it fell from 460 pixels to 345 when a hop turned out to spawn a new segment rather than move one, and from 345 to 0 when the segment left behind turned out to be destroyed a frame too early.

name: full-battle-loop
label: A whole battle end to end in the rollup ROM: the chip window a battle opens with, the BATTLE START! ribbon, the fight, the win, the RESULT window with its reward, and into the next battle's chip select. This loop did not exist before today -- the release build fielded four enemies that delete the navi in fifteen seconds and started the custom gauge empty, 1260 frames before the first chip. Every piece here is separately matched to the real ROM pixel for pixel.

name: battle-open-compare
label: How a battle opens, canon above and this build below. Found with the harness's first save state at a battle's FIRST frame, which immediately showed two things wrong here: a battle OPENS with the chip window (frame 165, unprompted) where this build made you wait 1260 frames for it, and BATTLE START! follows the chip window rather than the intro. Corrected, the banner lands at 291 against canon's 292.

name: wave-departure-compare
label: The Mettaur's shockwave, canon (sterile) left and this build right. A hop is not one sprite moving: the real ROM spawns a whole new segment on the next panel and the old one stops where it is, playing out its own animation until it comes back round to its last frame. The residue had been recorded as the virus holding its pickaxe too long -- its body is 0 pixels across all 70 frames. Now at 0: the last three frames were the departing segment being destroyed the instant its animation reached its final frame, rather than after that frame had been held for the duration it asks for -- the real ROM's own "last frame" flag is masked off until the frame's duration counter runs out, so it never means "reached", only "finished".

name: cursor-compare
label: The chip-select cursor walking OK to the fifth slot, canon left and this build right: 170 frames, 0 pixels. Everything the script drives -- the cursor, the card, the name -- was exact for a long time while the highlight bracket's blink stayed one frame out, and that was written off as unfixable: the blink counts from the window's opening, the canon side is a save state already open, so the two clocks were said to have no shared origin. Reading the routine instead of guessing at it settled it. The phase is (counter >> 3) & 1 off a frame counter in the window's own struct, window-relative on both sides -- the save state's value simply is not zero. The missing frame turned out to be ours: our slide-in reached its open state one frame after canon's does, invisible everywhere except in that blink.

name: banner-compare
label: The ENEMY DELETED banner, canon (sterile) above and this build below: 0 pixels over all 58 frames. The banner is text -- a font of 8x16 cells and a record per message, twenty cells uploaded as five 32x16 objects -- and all forty-five of the game's messages are in the build. The unrolling is one shared affine matrix whose vertical scale opens from a flat line, overshoots into a stretch, holds and rolls back up.
